dimensions.assessment: Affects political committees, campaigns, tax-exempt organizations, and federal government officers or employees.
dimensions.evidence: It shall be unlawful for any officer or employee of the United States, or any former officer or employee, willfully to disclose to any person... any information revealing the identification of any donor to a tax-exempt organization.

dimensions.assessment: Introduces felony criminal penalties, fines up to $250,000, and mandatory job dismissal for federal employees who violate donor privacy provisions.
dimensions.evidence: Any violation of this section shall be a felony punishable upon conviction by a fine in any amount not exceeding $250,000, or imprisonment of not more than 5 years, or both

dimensions.assessment: Negligible direct federal spending implications, though potential fine revenue and prosecution costs exist.
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act and imposes government-wide restrictions on handling tax-exempt donor records.
dimensions.evidence: An entity of the Federal Government may not collect or require the submission of information on the identification of any donor to a tax-exempt organization.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes to election laws and government recordkeeping restrictions.

missing_information: Number of entities or individuals expected to be prosecuted or investigated is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: Expands restrictions on foreign donations for election-related activities, adds certification and reporting requirements under the Federal Election Campaign Act, and restricts federal collection and disclosure of tax-exempt donor information with felony penalties for unauthorized disclosures.
